title: Crossbeam availability staffing scenario kit
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, practical kit for planning cross-functional staffing and escalation scenarios tied to availability SLOs. Intended audience: platform-engineering, SRE, serving-runtime, product-hosted-api, and solutions-eng. Use as a working doc during incident capacity planning and SLO rollout reviews.

Context / why now:
- Increasing surface area for model-serving has stretched oncall capacity; we need explicit staffing scenarios that map to SLO risk tiers.
- Customers (enterprise/Dedicated) expect predictable fallbacks and an escalation ladder when SLOs are threatened.
- We want a repeatable 30/60/90 runway for staffing experiments before formal SLO adoption.

Key objectives:
- Define discrete staffing scenarios (normal, constrained, degraded, surge) and the operational triggers for each.
- Map each scenario to concrete responsibilities across teams (who fires runbooks, who operates fallback routing, who owns customer comms).
- Provide a 30/90 day staffing ramp and experiment plan to validate handoffs and capacity assumptions.
- Capture open questions and automated metrics needed to evaluate success.

SLO surface (examples tied to scenarios):
- Availability SLO (p99 success rate): 99.9% per region (target for GA services).
- Latency SLO (p95 inference latency): <= 400ms for hosted-api small models; different tiers for large models/dedicated.
- Error budget burn alert thresholds: 5% (warning), 20% (action), 50% (escalate to exec bridge).

Staffing scenarios and triggers:
1) Normal (steady state)
- Trigger: error budget burn < 5% week-on-week; latency within accepted baselines.
- Staffing: Standard oncall rota (platform + serving-runtime). Primary oncall handles infra alerts; secondary is SRE pager.
- Actions: monitor dashboards, weekly cadence review.

2) Constrained capacity (identified risk)
- Trigger: sustained capacity pressure (e.g., container queueing, GPU pool saturation) or forecasted burst > 60% of spare capacity in 24h.
- Staffing: Add temporary coverage from platform-engineering (shift swap) + solutions-eng standby for customer-facing queues.
- Actions: throttle non-critical jobs, enable burst pool policy, run capacity scaling playbook (playbook reference below).

3) Degraded (SLO approaching breach)
- Trigger: error budget burn > 20% in rolling 1h window OR p95 latency degrades > 25% from baseline.
- Staffing: Trigger crossbeam bridge: platform-engineering lead, serving-runtime engineer, SRE incident commander, product-hosted-api PM for comms.
- Actions: execute immediate mitigations (fallback to smaller quantized model variants, enable prefix cache evictions), open incident ticket JIRA-ENG-####, notify CS for impacted customers.

4) Surge / Major outage
- Trigger: SLO breach detected (error budget > 50% or availability below target for > 15m) or cascading failures across regions.
- Staffing: Full incident bridge (IC + oncall + triage reps from each pillar + engineering director). Exec notification template used.
- Actions: follow incident runbook, invoke capacity emergency procedures, consider global routing fallback, start postmortem timeline.

Roles & responsibilities (quick map):
- Platform-engineering: capacity orchestration, autoscaler tuning, staffing coordination.
- Serving-runtime: model-level mitigations, kernel/quantization toggles, low-level debugging.
- SRE: incident commander, pager rotation, reliability instrumentation.
- Product-hosted-api: customer comms, rollback decisions, SLA notifications.
- Solutions/CS: customer triage and account-level mitigations.

30-day experiment plan (validation goals):
- Week 1: Tabletop run-through of Degraded scenario with oncall rotation mock bridge. Objectives: validate alert clarity, streamline runbook steps.
- Week 2-3: Simulated capacity stress test on staging (scale synthetic load to 1.5x baseline), measure alert precision and false positives.
- Week 4: Short retro and list of remediations (expected owners assigned).

90-day runway (staffing & deliverables):
- Month 1: Harden dashboards, finalize error budget thresholds, run two tabletop scenarios.
- Month 2: Implement automated routing fallback hooks and one-click model-variant swap in console (product + serving-runtime).
- Month 3: Run a controlled burst (canary) against Dedicated cluster, measure impact and finalize staffing rota changes.

Success metrics (how we know experiment worked):
- Alert-to-action time <= 5 minutes for Degraded scenario in 80% of runs.
- False positive incident rate < 10% during simulated stress tests.
- Customer-facing SLA incidents reduced by 50% quarter-over-quarter for targeted product routes.

Tactical checklists (copyable during a bridge):
- Whoever opens the bridge: create incident Jira, tag incident-ops, add timeline notes.
- IC: update the incident board every 15 minutes; record mitigations attempted and outcomes.
- Serving-runtime: attempt model-variant fallback (document model ids used).
- Platform-engineering: validate autoscaler logs, confirm new nodes/GPU pools are healthy.
- Product-hosted-api: draft customer advisory if expected impact > 30 minutes.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: insufficient cross-team staffing at night/weekends. Mitigation: create a reserve oncall pool (voluntary, compensated) and record handover templates.
- Risk: noisy alerts causing fatigue. Mitigation: refine thresholds, add debounce windows, and tag high-confidence signals only for bridge.
- Risk: model-variant rollback causes regressions. Mitigation: limited rollout, A/B validation with canary traffic, and quick revert commands in console.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What constitutes an acceptable p95 latency delta for each model family? (action: serving-runtime to propose per-model targets; owner: Maya)
- Leader sign-off for reserve oncall compensation policy (owner: Liam + People Ops).
- Finalize exec escalation threshold for enterprise accounts (owner: Product-hosted-api PM).

Quick links & runbooks to attach:
- Capacity scaling playbook: https://confluence.redwood.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=234523
- Incident bridge template: https://docs.google.com/templates/incident-bridge
- Runbook: model-variant fallback (ops-runbooks repo)

Immediate next steps (this doc as a working checklist):
- [ ] Platform-engineering to run Week 1 tabletop (owner: Asha) by 2026-03-12.
- [ ] Serving-runtime to draft per-model p95 proposals (owner: Maya) by 2026-03-20.
- [ ] SRE to draft reserve oncall rota proposal and cost estimate (owner: Liam) by 2026-03-18.
- [ ] Product to confirm customer advisory template and exec escalation cadence (owner: Jordan) by 2026-03-15.

Notes to self / scratch ideas:
- Consider an "availability scorecard" per account (score = weighted availability + latency + incident history) to drive proactive outreach.
- Automate deployment of a temporary cache hotspot when prefix cache miss rate increases beyond x%.

If you're reading this and want to run a scenario, ping #ops-runbooks and add a calendar slot with "Crossbeam scenario - tabletop".

Draft history: created 2026-02-10 by Asha Patel; iterated with Liam and Maya during platform sync 2026-03-04.
